svg.title: Japan at a glance
svg.desc: An editorial infographic about Japan: a stylized map with Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka and Nagoya; an overview; a bar chart of nominal GDP in current US dollars from 2015 to 2024; a donut chart of population by nationality; and highlights of places to visit.

g.text: A one-page primer on the Land of the Rising Sun
Geography, economy, people and places to see, in one view.
Japan is an archipelago in East Asia that stretches
some 3,000 km from the Sea of Okhotsk to the East China
Sea. Four main islands, Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu and
Shikoku, hold most of its land and people, while
mountains cover roughly three-quarters of the territory.
Life concentrates on narrow coastal plains, where the
Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya regions form one of the world's
Japan blends deep continuity with constant reinvention. A constitutional monarchy with the world's oldest
continuous hereditary dynasty, it modernised rapidly after 1868, rebuilt after 1945, and became a leader
in manufacturing, robotics and design. Today it faces an ageing, shrinking population (nearly 30% of
residents are 65 or older) while its food, pop culture and craftsmanship draw record numbers of visitors.
Japan is one of the world's largest
machinery and a vast services sector.

g.text: Sources: World Bank, GDP in current US$ (2015–2024); Statistics Bureau of Japan and Immigration Services Agency, population by nationality;
